verdict.root_cause: Frontend's gRPC calls to a backend at 172.18.0.24:7070 are being refused at the TCP layer (ECONNREFUSED, gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE) starting ~05:43:36, about one minute before the error-ratio change point at 05:44:46 on both frontend and frontend-proxy [tr_83aa4bdc809b, tr_c9826424f3bd, tr_39825163a4f0]. Nothing is listening on that port: the failure is immediate rejection, not slowness or saturation, and DNS resolved fine [tr_83aa4bdc809b]. Port 7070 matches the CART_ADDR value (cart:7071 was the transient override; the normal cart port is 7070) that platform-automation set and reverted ~1.4h before onset [tr_1faaffc58867], so the most likely culprit is the cart service process no longer accepting connections on its port while frontend holds a sticky, non-retried failed connection [tr_83aa4bdc809b]. The elevation is partial and bursty — only the request paths that touch this backend fail, which is why most traffic still succeeds [tr_39825163a4f0, tr_a469193f329f]. frontend-proxy and frontend are relays of this failure, not its source [tr_a469193f329f, tr_5be4a3a171b2].
verdict.reasoning: The only first-party error signal anywhere in the board is frontend's log: repeated gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE with ECONNREFUSED against a single resolved IP:port, beginning ~70s before the metric change point on both frontend and frontend-proxy. Connection-refused means the socket is closed, which excludes dependency_latency, process_freeze and network_partition (all of which hang rather than refuse) [tr_83aa4bdc809b]. frontend-proxy has no changes and shows negligible self-time with intact routing in sampled traces, so it is a propagation path, not the fault [tr_5be4a3a171b2, tr_a469193f329f]. frontend's only recorded changes are a set-and-revert of CART_ADDR completed 1.4h before onset, leaving the environment at its pre-change baseline — so the current config value is not itself wrong and bad_config is not the mechanism [tr_1faaffc58867]. That leaves the backend behind 172.18.0.24:7070 as the failing party. No specialist was dispatched against cart itself, so the mechanism on that host — crash-loop, OOM kill, bad artifact, or disk — is unidentified, which is why fault_class is unknown and confidence is low. Frontend's sticky cached connection failure [tr_83aa4bdc809b] explains why errors persist in bursts rather than clearing immediately, and the separate gRPC 13 INTERNAL from the email service on the shipping-quote path is a second, independent failure mode not covered by this verdict [tr_83aa4bdc809b].
open_questions: No dispatch ever examined the service behind 172.18.0.24:7070 — its identity must be confirmed (cart is inferred from the CART_ADDR port, not observed) and its logs, metrics, changes and restart history pulled to name the actual mechanism.
The second error family — gRPC 13 INTERNAL from an HTTP 400 returned by the email service on the shipping-quote path — is unexplained and may be an independent concurrent incident [tr_83aa4bdc809b].

frontend-proxy returned zero log lines across the entire window including the pre-onset period, so its log pipeline is broken or mislabelled; no absence-of-errors conclusion from the proxy is safe [tr_34f5c2d8163e], and the sampled traces contained no error spans at all [tr_a469193f329f], meaning the failing path was never captured in trace evidence.

alternatives.root_cause: The cart (or other 7070) backend exhausted memory or connections and was killed, so its listener disappeared and connections are refused.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and consistent with a refused socket, but no metric, log or change evidence was gathered from that host, so exhaustion is speculation rather than an observed mechanism.

alternatives.root_cause: A deploy of the 7070 backend shipped an artifact that cannot start, leaving nothing bound to the port.
alternatives.why_not: The change log was only queried for frontend-proxy and frontend; no deploy against the backend was ever looked for, and the set/revert of CART_ADDR at 04:34-04:43 is too distant from the 05:43 onset to supply the trigger [tr_1faaffc58867].

alternatives.root_cause: The CART_ADDR revert left frontend pointing at an address or port where no cart instance is listening, making the configuration value itself the failure.
alternatives.why_not: The revert restored the pre-04:34 baseline state and completed 1.4h before onset, with a quiet baseline in between — if the restored value were wrong, errors would have begun at 04:43, not 05:43 [tr_1faaffc58867, tr_c9826424f3bd].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so nothing should change: frontend's error ratio stays in its current bursty 0-30% band and the gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE / ECONNREFUSED 172.18.0.24:7070 lines continue or stop on their own (the log sample already ends at 05:53:34). The next observation that would unblock a proposal is a direct check of which container holds 172.18.0.24 and whether anything is bound to :7070, plus that service's own logs, restart count and change history.
proposal.if_wrong: If the identity check shows 172.18.0.24:7070 is in fact cart and cart's own evidence shows a crashed or non-listening process (restart count rising, no listener, its logs silent at 05:43:36), then abstaining was wrong and restart_service on cart becomes the right call. Equally, if the refusals persist past 06:11 and continue to drive the error ratio, the cost of waiting for identification becomes real.
proposal.risk: Abstention is not free: the refused-connection path keeps failing for the subset of requests that touch that backend, and if the process really is dead it stays dead until a human acts. I accept that cost because the only candidate action, restart_service on cart, rests on an inference the evidence actively contradicts: in the same incident window the sampled traces show cart serving AddItem/GetCart with Redis HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE leaves completing in 0.1-2.6ms with no errors [tr_a469193f329f], which is not consistent with cart refusing TCP connections. The 7070-means-cart link comes only from a CART_ADDR value that was set and reverted 1.4h before onset and was not in effect at onset [tr_1faaffc58867]. restart_service is also irreversible, so a restart aimed at the wrong service would discard that service's in-process cache, cause a connection reset for its callers, and leave the actual refused endpoint untouched while consuming the incident's remediation budget.
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal, since no change is made. For contrast, the action I am declining — restarting cart — would be seen by frontend (its only inbound caller in this graph) and therefore by frontend-proxy and load-generator traffic on the AddItem/GetCart paths, for the duration of the container recreate.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts span the proxy and frontend plus the load generator, indicating user-facing impact rather than a single quiet warning. No open incident covers it, and the cause could be any of several frontend dependencies, so a prior isn't warranted yet.
